name: Spite-Crucible
geological_features: Needle-thin volcanic vents ejecting metal-rich vapor
Collapsed magma chambers forming vast sinkholes
Surface crust thin enough to crack under moderate weight
description: Spite-Crucible is a small, treacherous volcanic world where the planetary crust is so thin that it flexes visibly under thermal stress, cracking open to reveal the molten interior beneath. Needle-thin volcanic vents pepper the surface, ejecting jets of metal-rich vapor that condense into glittering mineral deposits on the surrounding rock before the next eruption melts them down again.

The toxic atmosphere clings close to the surface, a thin, acrid layer that offers no protection from solar radiation while ensuring maximum discomfort for any sealed-suit operation. The planet seems designed to punish anyone who sets foot on it, each step a gamble on whether the crust will hold.

Collapsed magma chambers dot the landscape like open wounds, some stretching kilometers across and descending into darkness that thermal imaging cannot penetrate. Early probe data suggested these voids might contain stable environments, but every attempt to investigate has ended with the probe falling through a false floor into liquid rock.

Spite-Crucible has been classified as a navigational hazard rather than a resource opportunity, its mineral deposits too transient and its surface too unstable for any practical extraction. It serves primarily as a cautionary waypoint on stellar charts, a reminder that some worlds exist only to destroy what touches them.
